From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@brightlane.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:18 -0700
Subject: Intermittent latency spikes observed in inference calls (us-west-2)

Hi Karthik,

We're seeing intermittent latency spikes from calls to Redwood's hosted endpoint over the last 48 hours. Most requests return in ~120ms but a subset (about 2-3%) spike to 1.5–3s and are impacting our batch post-processing windows.

Example request IDs / timestamps (UTC):
- req_20260614_22:11:42 -> id: 7f2a1c
- req_20260615_01:08:09 -> id: 7f2a8d
- req_20260615_03:47:33 -> id: 7f31f0

We're on model: gptx-4-mini, region: us-west-2, avg seq len ~180 tokens. No body changes on our side; traffic pattern steady. Attached is a CSV with the 28 request IDs we captured and timestamps.

Can you confirm whether you're seeing any errors/capacity issues on your side? This is on our critical path, so any insight appreciated.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
SRE, Brightlane

Attachment: brightlane-sample-ids.csv (text/csv, 3 KB)

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the CSV, that's helpful. We're opening a short investigation. Next steps from our side:

1) Marissa will attempt to reproduce using your traffic shape and sequence-length distribution.
2) Monica will pull platform-side metrics (scheduling latency, queue depth, kernel time) for the time windows you provided.

If you can also share a couple of raw request payloads (anonymized is fine) and any client-side retry/backoff behavior, that will speed things up.

I can set up a 30-minute call this afternoon if you'd like to walk through specific request IDs. Otherwise we'll follow up in email with findings.

—Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:37:50 -0700
Subject: RE: Intermittent latency spikes observed in inference calls (us-west-2)

Karthik / Monica — quick summary of reproduction work done so far: 

- Replayed 3 traffic patterns matching Brightlane's CSV and seq-length distribution across a 24-hour window (burst + steady).
- Ran against gptx-4-mini pinned at the same model artifact; tested both cold-start and warmed KV cache scenarios.
- Observed 99th percentile latency at ~320ms across runs; occasional single requests up to ~540ms during synthetic scheduling jitter, but nothing in the 1–3s range.

Logs and artifacts attached: repro-run-20260615.log (contains traces for the synthetic requests) and repro-payloads.json (payloads used for replay). Notes from the run: the few high-latency samples correlate with brief GPU queueing spikes during concurrent autoscale events in the test cluster; with reduced concurrency those spikes disappear.

Conclusion: we could not reliably reproduce the 1.5–3s spikes using the provided samples and our replay. Next ask from Brightlane: any client-side proxies, retries, or network hops that might add latency.

Marissa
Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: repro-run-20260615.log (text/plain, 12 KB); repro-payloads.json (application/json, 9 KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@brightlane.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:22:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency spikes observed in inference calls (us-west-2)

Hi Alex — quick update from our investigation: 

- We replayed your sample traffic (see attached repro artifacts) against the same model and region; we did not observe the 1.5–3s outliers you reported. Our 99th percentile stayed under ~350ms in repeated runs.
- The small number of sub-second spikes we did see during stress runs appear tied to transient scheduling/queueing on the test cluster during autoscale events; those disappear if we lower concurrency.
- Platform metrics for the exact timestamps you provided show normal CPU/GPU utilization and no service-level errors.

What we need from you to proceed: 
- If possible, capture one full request/response trace for an instance of the spike (a curl with timing or a HAR) and the exact UTC timestamp (to the second). That will let us locate the server-side trace and correlate the request id.
- If the calls are routed through any proxy (CDN, internal API gateway), please confirm whether the timings you captured are client-side or server-side.

For transparency, we're keeping this open on our side as SUP-27614 so we can re-run targeted traces once we have a captured spike trace from Brightlane. If you prefer, we can do a short shared screen session to capture a trace in real time.

If we don't receive additional artifacts by EOD Thursday (2026-06-18), we'll close the internal investigation as "no reproducible evidence" and recommend reopening if it recurs.

Thanks — let me know how you'd like to proceed.

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
